About

A Little About Me

I'm a software developer who enjoys turning real-world problems into practical, working software. My core work is building backend systems with Java and Spring Boot — designing clean REST APIs, modelling databases, and wiring everything into responsive frontends that people actually enjoy using.

From a complete laundry management system to focused CRUD and API projects, I like owning a product end to end: database schema → API → interface → working software. I'm currently pursuing my M.Sc. in Computer Science while building full-stack projects that sharpen those skills every week.

  • Java programming & OOP
  • Spring Boot application development
  • REST API design & CRUD operations
  • Database design & SQL
  • Responsive frontend development
  • Modern development practices

Experience

My Development Journey

Not a job history — an honest map of how my skills were built, one layer at a time.

1
Foundation

Learning Java & Object-Oriented Programming

Started with core Java — classes, objects, inheritance, polymorphism and collections — building the mental model everything else stands on.

2
Backend

Building REST APIs with Spring Boot

Moved from plain Java to Spring Boot: controllers, services, repositories, dependency injection and clean layered architecture for real APIs.

3
Data

Working with SQL Databases

Designed schemas in MySQL and PostgreSQL — tables, keys, joins and relationships — and connected them to applications with JPA and Hibernate.

4
Applications

Developing CRUD Applications

Built complete create-read-update-delete systems with search, validation and structured error handling — tested end to end with Postman.

5
Frontend

Building Responsive Interfaces

Learned to pair backends with HTML, CSS and JavaScript interfaces that adapt cleanly from a phone screen to a desktop monitor.

6
Full-Stack · Now

Exploring Full-Stack Development

Building complete products end to end — most recently the Laundry Management System, designed and built solo and still growing feature by feature.

For Virendra — how to update this site

Profile photo: your headshot is shown in the hero card (assets/virendra-photo.png). To change it later, replace that file with a new portrait photo of the same name.

Project links: in the project data inside the page script, each project has a github field. Paste the real repo URL there and the “link to be added” slot in that project's details turns into a working Source Code button automatically. The Laundry Management System's GitHub link is already filled in.

Screenshots: the project visuals are lightweight built-in mockups. To use a real screenshot, save it under assets/ and swap the mock block in that project's card for an <img> pointing at it.

Numbers: the About statistics are the data-target values on the counters — edit them any time your project count grows.

Contact form: it composes a pre-filled email to your inbox via the visitor's mail app. To collect messages without that step, point the form at a form service (e.g. Formspree) later.
